# Introduction:

This report explains
the design of a DVD Loan Management System. The system is used to manage
borrowers, DVDs, loan records, and fines for overdue items. The report includes
database normalisation, an Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD), and SQL code used
to create and manage the database. It also shows queries used to retrieve,
update, and delete data.

# Database

Normalisation and its Advantages and Disadvantages:

**Normalisation**: Normalisation is the process of organising
data in a database to reduce redundancy and improve consistency.

**Advantages
of Normalisation**:
One advantage of normalisation is that it reduces data duplication in the
database. This means the same data is not stored in many places, which helps to
save storage space. Another advantage is that it improves data consistency,
because updating data in one place will update it correctly everywhere. This
makes the database more accurate and easier to manage (IBM, 2023).

**Disadvantages
of Normalisation**:
One disadvantage of normalisation is that it can make the database more
complex, because it creates many tables instead of one. This can make it harder
to understand for beginners. Another disadvantage is that queries can become
slower, because data must be joined from multiple tables, which takes more time
when retrieving information (IBM, 2023).

# Task

4- SQL Code and print screen of SQL output

**1) Query 1- Prints all
borrowers who have current rentals and order them by surname**  
SELECT DISTINCT b.BorrowerNo, b.BorrowerName, b.BorrowerAddress,
b.BorrowerStatus  
FROM Borrower b  
INNER JOIN Loan l ON b.BorrowerNo = l.BorrowerNo  
INNER JOIN LoanCopy lc ON l.LoanNo = lc.LoanNo  
INNER JOIN Copy c ON lc.CopyNo = c.CopyNo  
WHERE c.DVDStatus = 'On Loan'  
ORDER BY b.BorrowerName;

![](data:image/png;base64,)  

**2) Query 2-  Prints a list that shows all borrowers who have over-due loans and rank
them highest to lowest.**  
SELECT b.BorrowerNo, b.BorrowerName, *COUNT*(*) AS OverdueLoans  
FROM Borrower b  
INNER JOIN Loan l ON b.BorrowerNo = l.BorrowerNo  
INNER JOIN LoanCopy lc ON l.LoanNo = lc.LoanNo  
INNER JOIN Copy c ON lc.CopyNo = c.CopyNo  
WHERE c.DVDStatus = 'Overdue'  
GROUP BY b.BorrowerNo, b.BorrowerName  
ORDER BY OverdueLoans DESC;

![](data:image/png;base64,)  

**3)Query 3- Display the borrower details and
DVDs for all borrowers who have rented comedy movies in the last 4 weeks.  
**SELECT
b.BorrowerNo, b.BorrowerName, b.BorrowerAddress, d.DVDNo, d.DVDTitle,
l.LoanDate  
FROM Borrower b  
INNER JOIN Loan l ON b.BorrowerNo = l.BorrowerNo  
INNER JOIN LoanCopy lc ON l.LoanNo = lc.LoanNo  
INNER JOIN Copy c ON lc.CopyNo = c.CopyNo  
INNER JOIN DVD d ON c.DVDNo = d.DVDNo  
INNER JOIN RentalCategory rc ON d.CategoryID = rc.CategoryID  
WHERE rc.RentalCategory = 'Comedy'  
AND l.LoanDate >= *DATE_SUB*((SELECT *MAX*(LoanDate) FROM Loan),
INTERVAL 4 WEEK);  

![](data:image/png;base64,)

**4) Query 4 - the borrower
who has accumulate the most over-due finds, calculate the total in fines and
display their details.  
**SELECT
b.BorrowerNo, b.BorrowerName, b.BorrowerAddress, b.BorrowerStatus, *SUM*(f.Amount)
AS TotalFine  
FROM Borrower b  
INNER JOIN Loan l ON b.BorrowerNo = l.BorrowerNo  
INNER JOIN Fine f ON l.LoanNo = f.LoanNo  
WHERE f.PaidStatus = 'Unpaid'  
GROUP BY b.BorrowerNo, b.BorrowerName, b.BorrowerAddress, b.BorrowerStatus  
ORDER BY TotalFine DESC  
LIMIT 1;  

![](data:image/png;base64,)  
**5) Query 5- Update the cost for rentals where
the release date is >=2015 to £5.50 and the movie category is superhero.**  
UPDATE RentalCategory rc  
INNER JOIN DVD d ON rc.CategoryID = d.CategoryID  
SET rc.RentalCost = 5.50  
WHERE d.DVDYear >= 2015  
AND rc.RentalCategory = 'Superhero';  
SELECT * FROM RentalCategory  
WHERE RentalCategory = 'Superhero';  
![](data:image/png;base64,)  

**6) Query 6- Remove DVD movies from the system
where there are no loans registered for the movie**  
DELETE d  
FROM DVD d  
LEFT JOIN Copy c ON d.DVDNo = c.DVDNo  
WHERE c.DVDNo IS NULL;  

SELECT * FROM DVD;
